source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Finish the current treatment with the device before reporting the frayed cord because removal from service can wait until care is complete.","B":"Remove the damaged device from service and send it through the organization’s qualified inspection, repair, or replacement process before reuse.","C":"Cover the frayed section with adhesive tape and return the device to routine use if the equipment continues to function normally.","D":"Repair the cord at the bedside when no bare conductor is visible because clinical staff may correct minor electrical defects during use."}}
source_row.rationale: OSHA requires defective or damaged electrical equipment that may expose employees to injury to be removed from service until repaired and tested as safe.
source_row.source_detail: 29 CFR 1910.334(a)(2)(ii), Visual inspection — defective/damaged equipment removed from service until repaired and tested. eCFR/OSHA standard currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. source_row.stem: A nurse notices that an electrical medical device has a frayed power cord. What is the appropriate action?
